topics.title: Describe your room in 60 seconds
topics.description: Practice quick descriptive speaking about a familiar space.
topics.challenge_prompt: Describe your bedroom or living room for 60 seconds without stopping.
topics.objective: Building fluency with descriptive vocabulary
topics.opening_message: Let's warm up! Describe your room — furniture, colors, and how it feels — for 60 seconds. Ready? Go whenever you like.
topics.instructions: You used clear adjectives like 'cozy' and 'bright', nice work! Try adding more prepositions of place like 'next to' or 'behind' next time. Want to try again with more detail?
follow_up_directions: Describe your dream room instead
Describe your room in the past tense as it was as a child
Add three pieces of furniture you wish you had
Describe the room to someone who is blind
topics.evaluation_criteria: Uses at least 5 descriptive words and keeps talking for the full time

topics.title: Describe a person in 30 seconds
topics.description: Quickly describe someone's appearance and personality.
topics.challenge_prompt: In 30 seconds, describe a family member or friend's appearance and personality.
topics.objective: Using adjectives for appearance and character
topics.opening_message: Pick a person you know well and describe them for 30 seconds — how they look and what they're like. Go ahead!
topics.instructions: Great use of appearance words like 'tall' and 'curly hair'! Try adding a personality adjective too, like 'friendly' or 'funny'. Ready to describe another person?
follow_up_directions: Describe a famous person without naming them
Describe two people and compare them
Describe yourself instead
Guess who I'm describing based on clues you give
topics.grammar_focus: simple present with be and have
topics.evaluation_criteria: Mentions at least 2 appearance and 1 personality trait clearly

topics.title: Leave a 30-second voicemail
topics.description: Practice leaving a clear, polite voicemail message.
topics.challenge_prompt: Leave a 30-second voicemail for a friend explaining you'll be late to meet them.
topics.objective: Practicing polite spoken messages
topics.opening_message: Imagine you're calling a friend's voicemail to say you'll be late. Leave your message now — you have 30 seconds.
topics.instructions: Nice, you gave a clear reason for being late! Next time try adding a new meeting time at the end. Want to try a different voicemail scenario?
follow_up_directions: Leave a voicemail canceling plans entirely
Leave a voicemail for a doctor's office booking an appointment
Leave a voicemail apologizing for missing a call
Leave a formal voicemail for a job interview reschedule
topics.evaluation_criteria: Clearly states reason, new plan, and a polite closing

topics.title: Small talk sprint
topics.description: Keep a friendly small-talk conversation going without pausing.
topics.challenge_prompt: Talk about the weather and your weekend plans for 45 seconds, like small talk with a coworker.
topics.objective: Building casual conversation fluency
topics.opening_message: Let's practice small talk! Talk about the weather and your weekend plans for 45 seconds, like you're chatting with a coworker.
topics.instructions: Good energy and natural expressions like 'not bad, thanks'! Try asking a question back to keep the conversation two-way. Want another small talk topic?
follow_up_directions: Small talk about a recent holiday
Small talk while waiting in line at a coffee shop
Small talk with a new neighbor
Small talk at the start of a work meeting
topics.evaluation_criteria: Sounds natural and includes at least one question

topics.title: Give directions to your home
topics.description: Explain how to get somewhere using clear direction words.
topics.challenge_prompt: Give directions from the nearest bus stop to your home in 45 seconds.
topics.objective: Using direction vocabulary accurately
topics.opening_message: Imagine a friend is at the nearest bus stop and needs to reach your home. Give them directions in 45 seconds. Go!
topics.instructions: You used 'turn left' and 'straight ahead' really clearly! Try adding landmarks like 'next to the bank' to make it easier to follow. Want to try directions to a different place?
follow_up_directions: Give directions to the nearest supermarket
Give directions using only landmarks, no street names
Give directions for someone driving instead of walking
Give directions to a tourist who doesn't speak much English
topics.evaluation_criteria: Directions are logical and easy to follow step by step

topics.title: Tongue twister challenge
topics.description: Improve pronunciation clarity with tongue twisters.
topics.challenge_prompt: Say 'She sells seashells by the seashore' five times as clearly and quickly as you can within 30 seconds.
topics.objective: Improving pronunciation of tricky sound clusters
topics.opening_message: Time for a fun challenge! Say 'She sells seashells by the seashore' five times, as clearly as you can. You have 30 seconds — go!
topics.instructions: Your 's' and 'sh' sounds were nicely distinct! Try slowing down slightly on the third repetition where it got mixed up. Want to try a harder tongue twister?
follow_up_directions: Try 'Peter Piper picked a peck of pickled peppers'
Say the twister while smiling to affect the sound
Try it backward, word by word
Create your own tongue twister with 's' and 'th' sounds
topics.evaluation_criteria: Clear articulation of consonant clusters with minimal stumbling

topics.title: Linking sounds drill
topics.description: Practice connecting words smoothly like a native speaker.
topics.challenge_prompt: Say the phrase 'I want an apple and an orange' five times, linking the words smoothly.
topics.objective: Practicing consonant-to-vowel linking in natural speech
topics.opening_message: Let's smooth out your speech! Repeat 'I want an apple and an orange' five times, linking each word together naturally. Ready, go!
topics.instructions: Nice linking between 'want an'! Work on connecting 'and an' so it flows without a pause. Ready to try another linking phrase?
follow_up_directions: Try 'Turn it off and on again'
Try a full sentence with three linking points you choose
Practice linking with faster speed
Record yourself linking words in a random sentence
topics.evaluation_criteria: Words connect smoothly without unnatural pauses

topics.title: Speak without filler words
topics.description: Talk for 30 seconds avoiding 'um', 'like', and 'uh'.
topics.challenge_prompt: Talk about your favorite food for 30 seconds without saying 'um', 'uh', or 'like'.
topics.objective: Reducing filler word dependence in spoken English
topics.opening_message: Challenge time! Talk about your favorite food for 30 seconds, but avoid saying 'um', 'uh', or 'like'. Go ahead!
topics.instructions: You avoided fillers really well in the first half! I noticed one 'um' near the end — try pausing silently instead next time. Want to try a longer no-filler challenge?
follow_up_directions: Try 60 seconds without fillers on a harder topic
Talk about your job avoiding all fillers
Try describing a process without any fillers
Do it again but also avoid repeating any word twice
topics.evaluation_criteria: Zero or minimal filler words used across the full response

topics.title: Question-forming sprint
topics.description: Quickly form correct questions about a given topic.
topics.challenge_prompt: In 30 seconds, ask as many correct questions as you can about traveling abroad.
topics.objective: Practicing rapid, accurate question formation
topics.opening_message: Let's sprint! In 30 seconds, ask as many correct questions as you can about traveling abroad. Ready, set, go!
topics.instructions: You formed several great questions with correct word order! One question was missing the auxiliary verb — remember 'do' or 'does' in present simple questions. Want another sprint round?
follow_up_directions: Sprint again on the topic of cooking
Only ask questions using the past tense
Ask only yes/no questions this time
Ask five questions to a job interviewer
topics.evaluation_criteria: Grammatically correct questions with proper word order

topics.title: 30-second elevator pitch
topics.description: Introduce yourself and your goal concisely.
topics.challenge_prompt: Give a 30-second elevator pitch introducing yourself and one goal you have.
topics.objective: Delivering concise self-introductions
topics.opening_message: Imagine you're in an elevator with someone important. Give a 30-second pitch about who you are and one goal you have. Go!
topics.instructions: Great, confident opening line! Try ending with a clear call to action, like asking for their contact info. Want to try pitching a different goal?
follow_up_directions: Pitch a business idea instead of yourself
Pitch yourself for a specific job role
Make the pitch only 15 seconds
Pitch to a skeptical listener who interrupts you
topics.grammar_focus: present simple and future with will
topics.evaluation_criteria: Concise, confident, and includes a clear goal statement

topics.title: Explain a process step by step
topics.description: Explain how to make coffee or tea clearly using sequencing words.
topics.challenge_prompt: Explain how to make your favorite hot drink, step by step, in 60 seconds.
topics.objective: Using sequencing language to explain a process
topics.opening_message: Let's practice explaining processes! Tell me, step by step, how to make your favorite hot drink. You have 60 seconds.
topics.instructions: You used great sequencing words like 'first' and 'then'! Try adding a warning or tip, like 'be careful not to burn it'. Want to explain a different process?
follow_up_directions: Explain how to change a flat tire
Explain a process from your job
Explain it as if teaching a five-year-old
Explain the same process but skip a step on purpose and see if I notice
topics.evaluation_criteria: Clear logical steps using at least 4 sequencing words

topics.title: 90-second monologue about a hobby
topics.description: Speak continuously about a hobby for 90 seconds.
topics.challenge_prompt: Talk about a hobby you enjoy for 90 seconds without stopping.
topics.objective: Sustaining fluent speech on a familiar topic
topics.opening_message: Let's build stamina! Talk about a hobby you love for 90 seconds straight, no long pauses. Whenever you're ready, begin.
topics.instructions: You kept great momentum throughout, well done! I noticed a few long pauses near the middle — try using a filler phrase like 'what's more' to bridge ideas. Want to try 90 seconds on another hobby?
follow_up_directions: Talk about a hobby you dislike and why
Talk for 120 seconds on the same hobby with more detail
Explain how you'd teach this hobby to a beginner
Compare this hobby to another one you tried once
topics.evaluation_criteria: Speaks fluently for the full duration with minimal unnatural pauses

topics.title: Retell a story in past tense
topics.description: Retell a recent event using correct past tense forms.
topics.challenge_prompt: Retell something interesting that happened to you last week, using past tense, in 60 seconds.
topics.objective: Practicing accurate past tense narration
topics.opening_message: Tell me about something interesting that happened to you last week. Use the past tense and take 60 seconds to tell the story.
topics.instructions: Your story had a clear beginning and end, nice structure! I noticed one irregular verb error with 'goed' instead of 'went' — worth double-checking those. Ready to retell another story?
follow_up_directions: Retell the same story in present tense as if it's happening now
Retell a story from someone else's perspective
Add a surprising twist to the story
Retell a childhood memory instead
topics.evaluation_criteria: Accurate past tense forms with a clear narrative arc

topics.title: Agree or disagree politely
topics.description: Practice polite disagreement phrases on a debatable topic.
topics.challenge_prompt: Respond to the statement 'Working from home is better than working in an office' by politely agreeing or disagreeing, in 60 seconds.
topics.objective: Using polite disagreement and agreement phrases
topics.opening_message: Here's a statement: 'Working from home is better than working in an office.' Agree or disagree politely and explain why, in 60 seconds.
topics.instructions: You used a nice softening phrase, 'I see your point, but...' Try adding a specific example to strengthen your argument next time. Want to respond to another statement?
follow_up_directions: Respond to 'Social media does more harm than good'
Argue the opposite side of your original opinion
Do it again but disagree strongly and firmly
Respond as if talking to your boss instead of a friend
topics.grammar_focus: modal verbs for opinion, e.g. I think, I'd say
topics.evaluation_criteria: Polite tone with a clear stance and supporting reason

topics.title: Summarize a news story
topics.description: Summarize a recent news event clearly and concisely.
topics.challenge_prompt: Summarize a news story you read or heard recently in 60 seconds.
topics.objective: Practicing concise summarizing skills
topics.opening_message: Think of a news story you saw recently — local, world, or sports. Summarize it in 60 seconds, covering the key facts.
topics.instructions: Good job covering who, what, and where! Try adding when it happened for a more complete summary. Want to summarize another story?
follow_up_directions: Summarize the story in only 20 seconds
Summarize it as a headline plus two sentences
Give your opinion on the story after summarizing
Summarize a story from a topic you know little about
topics.evaluation_criteria: Covers key facts concisely within the time limit

topics.title: Give a sincere apology
topics.description: Practice a natural, sincere spoken apology.
topics.challenge_prompt: Apologize to a friend for forgetting their birthday, speaking for 45 seconds.
topics.objective: Practicing sincere apology language
topics.opening_message: You forgot your friend's birthday! Apologize to them sincerely, and explain what happened, in 45 seconds.
topics.instructions: Your apology sounded genuine and you took responsibility clearly! Adding a specific way to make it up to them would make it even stronger. Want to apologize for a different situation?
follow_up_directions: Apologize to a boss for missing a deadline
Apologize for a mistake you didn't fully cause
Apologize in a formal, written-style tone
Apologize and have the listener not fully accept it, then respond
topics.grammar_focus: past tense and conditionals for hypothetical fixes
topics.evaluation_criteria: Sincere tone, clear reason, and an offer to make amends

topics.title: Make a 45-second complaint
topics.description: Politely complain about poor service in a restaurant.
topics.challenge_prompt: Politely complain to a waiter about a cold meal, speaking for 45 seconds.
topics.objective: Practicing polite complaint language
topics.opening_message: Your meal arrived cold at a restaurant. Politely complain to the waiter and ask for a solution, in 45 seconds.
topics.instructions: You stayed polite while clearly stating the problem, well done! Try suggesting a specific solution, like a replacement or discount. Want to try complaining about something else?
follow_up_directions: Complain about a delayed flight
Complain about a noisy neighbor
Complain firmly but rudely, then redo it politely
Complain in writing style as if for an email
topics.grammar_focus: modal verbs for requests, could you, would you
topics.evaluation_criteria: States the problem clearly and remains polite throughout

topics.title: Give advice to a friend
topics.description: Offer clear spoken advice using modal verbs.
topics.challenge_prompt: A friend is stressed about a job interview. Give them advice for 60 seconds.
topics.objective: Practicing advice-giving language
topics.opening_message: Your friend has a big job interview tomorrow and is nervous. Give them advice for 60 seconds to help them feel ready.
topics.instructions: Your advice was practical, especially the tip about preparing questions! Try using 'should' or 'why don't you' to vary your advice phrasing. Want to give advice on another situation?
follow_up_directions: Give advice to someone learning a new language
Give advice about a health problem
Give advice, but the friend disagrees with each suggestion
Give advice to your younger self
topics.evaluation_criteria: Offers at least two clear, practical pieces of advice

topics.title: Explain a mistake you made
topics.description: Describe a past mistake and what you learned.
topics.challenge_prompt: Describe a mistake you made at work or school, and what you learned from it, in 60 seconds.
topics.objective: Reflecting on experience using past tense and lesson-learned language
topics.opening_message: Tell me about a mistake you made at work or school and what you learned from it. You have 60 seconds.
topics.instructions: You explained the situation clearly and honestly! Adding how you'd handle it differently now would round out the reflection nicely. Want to share another mistake story?
follow_up_directions: Explain a mistake someone else made that affected you
Explain the same mistake as if defending yourself
Turn the mistake into advice for someone else
Describe a mistake you're still worried about
topics.evaluation_criteria: Clear explanation with an honest reflection or lesson

topics.title: Compare two options
topics.description: Compare living in a city versus a small town.
topics.challenge_prompt: Compare living in a big city versus a small town for 60 seconds, then say which you prefer.
topics.objective: Using comparative language to evaluate options
topics.opening_message: Compare living in a big city versus a small town for 60 seconds, and tell me which you'd choose and why.
topics.instructions: You used comparatives like 'more convenient' really naturally! Try adding a superlative, like 'the best part of...' to strengthen your conclusion. Want to compare two different options?
follow_up_directions: Compare two jobs you could take
Compare two smartphones or gadgets
Compare renting versus buying a home
Compare two vacation destinations
topics.evaluation_criteria: Uses at least two comparative structures and gives a clear preference

topics.title: Make predictions about the future
topics.description: Predict what technology will look like in 20 years.
topics.challenge_prompt: Predict what technology will be like in 20 years, speaking for 60 seconds.
topics.objective: Using future forms to express predictions
topics.opening_message: What do you think technology will look like in 20 years? Share your predictions for 60 seconds.
topics.instructions: Great use of 'will' for confident predictions! Try adding 'might' or 'could' for less certain ideas to show a range of confidence. Want to predict something else?
follow_up_directions: Predict the future of your own career
Predict how your city will change
Predict the outcome of a current event
Make predictions you're not confident about and explain why
topics.evaluation_criteria: Uses varied future forms to express different levels of certainty

topics.title: Describe data verbally
topics.description: Describe a simple trend, like rising coffee prices, in spoken form.
topics.challenge_prompt: Describe how coffee prices have changed over the last five years, as if reading a chart, in 60 seconds.
topics.objective: Using trend vocabulary to describe data aloud
topics.opening_message: Imagine a chart showing coffee prices rising steadily over five years, with a dip in year three. Describe this trend aloud for 60 seconds.
topics.instructions: You described the overall rise clearly! Try adding specific trend verbs like 'plummeted' or 'leveled off' for the dip. Want to describe a different data trend?
follow_up_directions: Describe a trend that goes up, then sharply down
Describe population growth in a country
Describe your own spending habits as a trend
Describe a trend using percentages
topics.grammar_focus: present perfect for change over time
topics.evaluation_criteria: Accurately narrates the trend direction using appropriate vocabulary

topics.title: Define an abstract word
topics.description: Define and give an example of the word 'success'.
topics.challenge_prompt: Define the word 'success' in your own words and give a personal example, in 45 seconds.
topics.objective: Practicing abstract definitions with examples
topics.opening_message: What does 'success' mean to you? Define it in your own words and give a personal example, in 45 seconds.
topics.instructions: Your definition was thoughtful and personal! Try adding a contrasting idea, like what success is not, to sharpen the definition. Want to define another abstract word?
follow_up_directions: Define 'freedom' instead
Define 'happiness' and compare it to 'success'
Define a word you find hard to explain
Define a word only using examples, no direct definition
topics.evaluation_criteria: Clear definition supported by a relevant personal example

topics.title: Use three given idioms
topics.description: Naturally include three idioms in a short story.
topics.challenge_prompt: Tell a short story that naturally uses these three idioms: 'break the ice', 'hit the road', and 'piece of cake', in 60 seconds.
topics.objective: Using idioms naturally in context
topics.opening_message: Here are three idioms: 'break the ice', 'hit the road', and 'piece of cake'. Tell a short story using all three naturally, in 60 seconds.
topics.instructions: You used 'break the ice' perfectly in context! 'Piece of cake' felt a bit forced — try connecting it more smoothly to the sentence before it. Want to try three new idioms?
follow_up_directions: Try idioms: 'under the weather', 'costs an arm and a leg', 'once in a blue moon'
Use the same three idioms in a work context instead
Use four idioms this time
Explain the literal meaning behind each idiom afterward
topics.evaluation_criteria: All three idioms used correctly and naturally in context

topics.title: Persuade someone to try something new
topics.description: Convince a friend to try a new restaurant or activity.
topics.challenge_prompt: Persuade a friend to try a new restaurant with you this weekend, speaking for 60 seconds.
topics.objective: Using persuasive language and rhetorical techniques
topics.opening_message: Try to persuade a friend to come to a new restaurant with you this weekend. You have 60 seconds to convince them.
topics.instructions: You built a strong case with specific reasons, nice! Adding a rhetorical question, like 'wouldn't it be fun to try something new?' could make it even more persuasive. Want to persuade about something else?
follow_up_directions: Persuade someone to switch careers
Persuade a skeptical audience about a controversial idea
Persuade in a formal business pitch style
Persuade someone who keeps saying no, and adapt your approach
topics.grammar_focus: conditionals for persuasion, if you..., you'll
topics.evaluation_criteria: Uses persuasive techniques and sounds convincing overall

topics.title: Hypothetical: winning the lottery
topics.description: Talk about what you'd do if you won the lottery.
topics.challenge_prompt: Explain what you would do if you won the lottery tomorrow, in 60 seconds, using hypothetical language.
topics.objective: Practicing second conditional structures
topics.opening_message: Imagine you won the lottery tomorrow. What would you do? Tell me for 60 seconds using 'would' and 'if'.
topics.instructions: Your conditional structures were solid throughout! Try adding a third idea building on the first two for a richer response. Want another hypothetical scenario?
follow_up_directions: Discuss what you'd do if you could travel anywhere for free
Discuss what you'd do if you lost your job tomorrow
Discuss a hypothetical from your childhood, 'if I had known...'
Combine second and third conditionals in one answer
topics.evaluation_criteria: Correct use of second conditional with logical, varied ideas

topics.title: Stress and intonation drill
topics.description: Practice changing meaning by shifting word stress.
topics.challenge_prompt: Say the sentence 'I didn't say she stole the money' five times, stressing a different word each time, and explain how the meaning changes.
topics.objective: Practicing meaning changes through stress and intonation
topics.opening_message: Say 'I didn't say she stole the money' five times, stressing a different word each time, and briefly explain how the meaning shifts. Go ahead!
topics.instructions: Your stress shifts were clear on the first three attempts! The stress on 'money' was a bit subtle — try emphasizing it more strongly. Want to try a new sentence for this drill?
follow_up_directions: Try the drill with 'I never said he was lying'
Do the drill using only rising intonation each time
Do the drill using questions instead of statements
Create your own sentence for the stress drill
topics.evaluation_criteria: Clearly shifts stress and accurately explains meaning changes

topics.title: Speed vocabulary challenge
topics.description: List as many words as possible in a category within 30 seconds.
topics.challenge_prompt: In 30 seconds, name as many words related to 'the kitchen' as you can.
topics.objective: Rapidly retrieving topic-specific vocabulary
topics.opening_message: Ready for a speed round? In 30 seconds, name as many kitchen-related words as you can. Go!
topics.instructions: Excellent range of words, from appliances to utensils! Try grouping words by category next time to recall even more quickly. Want to try another category?
follow_up_directions: Try the same challenge with 'the office'
Try naming only verbs related to cooking
Try naming words starting with a specific letter
Do it again but describe each word's use briefly
topics.evaluation_criteria: Produces a high number of accurate, relevant words quickly

topics.title: 1-minute presentation on a topic
topics.description: Give a structured one-minute presentation on a chosen topic.
topics.challenge_prompt: Give a structured 60-second presentation about the benefits of exercise, with an intro, two points, and a conclusion.
topics.objective: Practicing structured presentation delivery
topics.opening_message: Give a 60-second presentation on the benefits of exercise. Include a short intro, two main points, and a conclusion. Ready, go!
topics.instructions: Your structure was very clear, with a strong intro and conclusion! Try adding a transition word like 'furthermore' between your two points. Want to present on another topic?
follow_up_directions: Present on the benefits of reading instead
Present with three points instead of two
Present as if to a skeptical audience
Present the same topic in only 30 seconds
topics.evaluation_criteria: Clear structure with intro, supporting points, and conclusion

topics.title: Argue for and against a topic
topics.description: Present both sides of an argument on remote learning.
topics.challenge_prompt: Argue both for and against online learning being better than classroom learning, in 90 seconds total.
topics.objective: Presenting balanced arguments on both sides
topics.opening_message: Take 90 seconds to argue both for and against online learning being better than classroom learning — give both sides fairly.
topics.instructions: You presented the 'for' side with strong examples! The 'against' side was shorter — try balancing the time more evenly between both sides. Want to argue a different topic both ways?
follow_up_directions: Argue both sides of 'social media is good for society'
Argue both sides but end with your personal opinion
Argue only the side you personally disagree with
Debate this topic as if responding to a rebuttal
topics.vocabulary_focus: argumentative connectors, on one hand, on the other hand
topics.grammar_focus: present simple and modal verbs for opinion
topics.evaluation_criteria: Balanced, well-supported arguments on both sides

topics.title: 120-second monologue about travel
topics.description: Speak continuously for two minutes about a memorable trip.
topics.challenge_prompt: Talk about a memorable trip you took, for a full 120 seconds without stopping.
topics.objective: Sustaining extended fluent speech with detail
topics.opening_message: Tell me about a memorable trip you took. You have 120 seconds to describe it in detail — where, what happened, and how you felt.
topics.instructions: You maintained great fluency and included vivid sensory details! Try varying your sentence openings more, since several started with 'and then'. Want to try another 120-second story?
follow_up_directions: Talk about a trip that went wrong
Talk about a trip you wish you could take
Retell the trip from a companion's point of view
Add a piece of dialogue from the trip into your story
topics.grammar_focus: past tenses combined, simple past and past continuous
topics.evaluation_criteria: Sustains fluent, detailed speech for the full two minutes

topics.title: Spontaneous opinion challenge
topics.description: Give an immediate opinion on a surprise topic.
topics.challenge_prompt: Give your immediate opinion on whether zoos should exist, speaking for 45 seconds with no preparation time.
topics.objective: Practicing quick, unrehearsed opinion delivery
topics.opening_message: No time to prepare — should zoos exist? Give me your honest opinion right now for 45 seconds.
topics.instructions: You jumped in confidently with a clear stance! Try backing it up with one concrete example or fact next time. Want another spontaneous topic?
follow_up_directions: Give a spontaneous opinion on remote work
Give a spontaneous opinion, then argue the opposite immediately
Give an opinion on a topic you know very little about
Give your opinion in exactly three sentences
topics.vocabulary_focus: opinion phrases, in my view, I believe
topics.evaluation_criteria: Clear, immediate stance supported by at least one reason

topics.title: Explain a graph trend in detail
topics.description: Describe a fluctuating sales graph with reasons for the changes.
topics.challenge_prompt: Describe a sales graph that rises in spring, drops in summer, and rises again in winter, explaining possible reasons, in 90 seconds.
topics.objective: Combining data description with reasoning
topics.opening_message: Imagine a company's sales rise in spring, drop in summer, then rise again in winter. Describe this trend and suggest reasons why, in 90 seconds.
topics.instructions: Your trend description was accurate and well-paced! Your reasoning for the summer drop was strong — try adding a reason for the winter increase too. Want to describe another trend with reasoning?
follow_up_directions: Describe a stock price trend with causes
Describe a temperature graph over a year
Describe website traffic trends for a business
Describe a trend and predict what happens next
topics.evaluation_criteria: Accurately describes the trend and gives plausible reasons

topics.title: Debate rebuttal practice
topics.description: Respond to a counterargument with a strong rebuttal.
topics.challenge_prompt: Someone argues 'AI will take all our jobs, so we should stop developing it.' Give a 90-second rebuttal.
topics.objective: Constructing logical rebuttals under time pressure
topics.opening_message: Here's an argument: 'AI will take all our jobs, so we should stop developing it.' Give a 90-second rebuttal challenging this view.
topics.instructions: Your rebuttal addressed the core assumption really effectively! Try acknowledging one valid point from the original argument before countering, for a more balanced tone. Want to rebut another claim?
follow_up_directions: Rebut the claim that 'money can't buy happiness'
Rebut an argument you personally agree with
Give a rebuttal, then a rebuttal to your own rebuttal
Deliver the rebuttal in a calm, diplomatic tone only
topics.evaluation_criteria: Logical, well-structured rebuttal addressing the core claim

topics.title: Nuanced comparison of two philosophies
topics.description: Compare individualism and collectivism with nuance.
topics.challenge_prompt: Compare individualism and collectivism as cultural values, discussing strengths and weaknesses of each, in 120 seconds.
topics.objective: Discussing abstract concepts with nuance and balance
topics.opening_message: Compare individualism and collectivism as cultural values — strengths and weaknesses of each — for 120 seconds.
topics.instructions: Your analysis showed real nuance, especially acknowledging context-dependence! Try adding a real-world example to ground the abstract ideas. Want to compare another pair of concepts?
follow_up_directions: Compare optimism and realism as life philosophies
Compare capitalism and socialism with nuance
Argue which philosophy suits modern life better, with justification
Present the comparison as if writing an academic abstract
topics.evaluation_criteria: Balanced, nuanced discussion with clear structure and examples

topics.title: Give an impromptu wedding toast
